before: rustc translates a Rust source file into an executable. Editing main.rs does not change an already-built executable.
This course uses stable Rust 1.99.1 with edition 2024. An edition is not the same thing as a compiler version; one compiler can support several editions.
Cargo reads a manifest named Cargo.toml. The early single-file examples can also be compiled directly with rustc.
These fixtures need no downloaded crates or nightly features. The app shows concepts and checks rather than a Rust browser runner.
Expected output or behavior: Ready. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: In a new folder save main.rs, run rustc --edition=2024 main.rs -o lesson, then ./lesson. Compare running before and after rebuilding an edited message. You may trace it without a Rust compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: Source code is the text you edit. `rustc`, the Rust compiler, turns it into a file the computer can run. Editing the source does not update a file you already built.
An edition chooses a set of Rust language rules. These examples use edition 2024 with Rust 1.99.1. A compiler version and a language edition are different; one compiler can support several editions.
Cargo is Rust's project tool. It reads project settings from Cargo.toml. For this single file, rustc can build the program directly.
You can read the example here or run it with Rust installed on your computer. These examples use stable Rust and do not need extra downloaded libraries.
The program shows `Ready` when the built file runs.

To try it, save the example as main.rs in a new folder. In a terminal there, use `rustc --edition=2024 main.rs -o lesson.exe`. Run `.\lesson.exe` in Windows PowerShell or `./lesson.exe` on macOS or Linux. After editing the message, build again to include the change.

before.question: After editing the message, you run the previous executable without rebuilding. What can appear?
choices: The old message from the earlier compilation.
The new source must be interpreted automatically.
before.explanation: Source edits and executable generation are separate steps.

after.question: Edit the message, then run the old file without rebuilding. What can appear?
choices: The message from the earlier build.
The new source always runs automatically.
after.explanation: The old file still contains the old instructions. Editing the source alone does not rebuild it.
